c.tagline: Zambia's gateway to Victoria Falls, where the Zambezi thunders into the mist.

taxi.fareNote: There is no Uber or Bolt in Livingstone and taxis are unmetered — agree the fare before getting in. Most visitors use lodge-arranged transfers or booked activity operators rather than hailing on the street.

emergency.note: 112 also reaches emergency services from most mobile phones; response times can be slow, and many visitors rely on their lodge or a private clinic first.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Don't walk the road to the Falls or along the Zambezi at dusk — elephants roam freely, and petty theft occurs around the market.

hood_desc: The compact grid along Mosi-oa-Tunya Road with the Livingstone Museum, Mukuni Park curio market, banks, restaurants and most backpacker lodges; the convenient walkable base for first-timers.
The lush strip of luxury lodges lining the Zambezi upstream of the falls, home to sunset cruises, spa resorts and riverfront game lawns; best for travellers wanting comfort and calm on the water.

The southern gateway toward the Mosi-oa-Tunya (Victoria Falls) National Park entrance and the Zambezi rainforest, dotted with safari lodges and activity operators for rafting, bungee and Devil's Pool.
A traditional township east of the centre around the Maramba market and the Maramba Cultural Museum, with local eateries, drumming and dance; an authentic, budget-friendly, less touristy feel.
A quiet residential suburb of guesthouses and self-catering homes north of the centre, good for families and longer stays wanting a relaxed local pace away from the tourist strip.
lodging: The Royal Livingstone Victoria Falls Hotel by Anantara
The David Livingstone Safari Lodge & Spa

water.note: Town supply is chlorinated but quality varies — most visitors stick to bottled or filtered water.

transit.hours: Shared minibuses run roughly 6:00 AM to early evening; after dark you rely on taxis or a prearranged transfer.
transit.note: Livingstone has no metro, tram or city bus network. Shared minibuses ply the main routes cheaply, while taxis and lodge transfers cover the tourist sites and airport.
transit.pay: Minibus and taxi fares are paid in cash (Zambian Kwacha) directly to the driver or conductor; there is no transit card. US dollars are widely accepted for tours and lodges.

bus: Intercity coaches to Lusaka (Mazhandu Family Bus, Shalom) and cross-border services to Botswana, Namibia and Zimbabwe
train: Zambia Railways passenger service to Lusaka (slow, infrequent)

transit.m: Taxi to town centre (~15 min); most lodges offer prearranged airport transfers
Hotel shuttle / prearranged transfer to riverfront lodges (~20 min)

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants is appreciated for good service; tipping safari guides, drivers and porters is customary in the tourism trade.

food.name: Nshima with relish
food.desc: Zambia's staple: a stiff white maize meal pudding eaten by hand, scooped with a relish of greens, beans, beef stew or fish.

places.name: Cafe Zambezi
places.note: Livingstone's best-known local kitchen; nshima plates with a choice of relish, long a backpacker favourite.

places.name: Zest Bar and Restaurant
places.note: Consistently well-reviewed spot serving Zambian nshima plates alongside grills in a garden setting.

places.name: Maramba Market food stalls
places.note: Cook stalls dish nshima with beans, greens and stew for a few kwacha; the most authentic, cheapest version.

food.name: Game meat grill
food.desc: Kudu, impala, warthog and crocodile steaks grilled over coals, a Livingstone specialty served with nshima or chips.

places.name: Cafe Zambezi
places.note: Famous for its game platter of crocodile, kudu and impala; the classic first-night meal in town.

places.name: Zest Bar and Restaurant
places.note: Kudu, impala and crocodile appear regularly on the grill menu at fair prices.

places.name: The Royal Livingstone Hotel dining room
places.note: Upmarket game cuts served with Zambezi views and resident zebra on the lawn.

food.name: Kapenta
food.desc: Tiny sun-dried freshwater sardines fried crisp with tomato and onion, a salty, protein-rich relish for nshima.

places.name: Maramba Market food stalls
places.note: Sold dried by the scoop and cooked to order at the market kitchens; the everyday Zambian way to eat it.

places.name: Cafe Zambezi
places.note: Puts kapenta on its traditional Zambian menu for visitors who want it without market hunting.

places.name: Livingstone Town Market
places.note: Stacks of dried kapenta plus stalls frying it fresh; good for a cheap lunch among locals.

food.name: Village chicken
food.desc: Free-range chicken slow-stewed with tomato, onion and chilli until it falls off the bone; leaner and far tastier than farmed birds.

places.name: Cafe Zambezi
places.note: Village chicken stew with nshima is the house standard-bearer for Zambian home cooking.

places.name: Rite Pub and Grill
places.note: Popular local pub grill where chicken and nshima come cheap, loud and busy in the evenings.

places.name: Maramba Market food stalls
places.note: Braai stalls turn out grilled village chicken over open coals through the afternoon.

food.name: Ifisashi
food.desc: Pumpkin leaves, rape or cassava greens simmered in groundnut sauce; the classic vegetarian relish alongside nshima.

places.name: Cafe Zambezi
places.note: Groundnut greens served as a side or as a full vegetarian nshima plate.

places.name: Maramba Market food stalls
places.note: Every cook stall makes it daily; ask for nshima na chibwabwa for the pumpkin-leaf version.

places.name: Olga's Italian Corner
places.note: Community-run kitchen mixing Italian plates with Zambian greens and stews; profits fund a local youth project.

food.name: Zambezi bream
food.desc: Whole tilapia from the Zambezi, grilled or deep-fried and served with nshima, chips and a squeeze of lemon.

places.name: The Waterfront
places.note: Riverside deck at David Livingstone Safari Lodge; grilled bream eaten at sunset over the Zambezi.

places.name: Zest Bar and Restaurant
places.note: Whole grilled bream is a menu regular and one of the better-value fish plates in town.

places.name: Livingstone Town Market
places.note: Fresh river fish sold each morning and fried on the spot at neighbouring stalls.

food.name: Mosi Lager
food.desc: Zambia's national beer, named for Mosi-oa-Tunya, the Smoke that Thunders; a light, crisp lager brewed for the heat.

places.name: Fez Bar
places.note: Long-running Livingstone bar and the town's default cold-Mosi meeting point after a day at the Falls.

places.name: The Waterfront
places.note: Sundowner Mosi on the Zambezi deck, with hippos usually in earshot.

places.name: Rite Pub and Grill
places.note: Unfussy local pub where Mosi is cheapest and the crowd is entirely Zambian.

food.name: Maheu
food.desc: Thick, lightly sweet non-alcoholic maize drink sold chilled by the carton; a Zambian everyday refresher and a filling snack in itself.

places.name: Maramba Market
places.note: Sold ice-cold at nearly every stall, in banana, strawberry and plain maize flavours.

places.name: Livingstone Town Market
places.note: Cheapest place to try maheu plus the traditional munkoyo root drink when in season.

places.name: Cafe Zambezi
places.note: Serves maheu and other local non-alcoholic drinks alongside the Zambian food menu.

landmarks: Victoria Falls (Mosi-oa-Tunya)
'The Smoke That Thunders' plunges the entire Zambezi over a 108-meter chasm, a UNESCO wonder whose spray plume is visible from twenty kilometers away.
Knife-Edge Bridge
This narrow footbridge thrusts visitors into the falls' drenching spray for the most dramatic face-on views of the Eastern Cataract and boiling gorge below.
Devil's Pool and Livingstone Island
In low-water season, daredevils swim to a natural rock pool perched on the very lip of Victoria Falls, from the island where David Livingstone first gazed over the edge.
Victoria Falls Bridge
Cecil Rhodes' elegant 1905 steel arch spans the Second Gorge between Zambia and Zimbabwe, offering bungee jumps and knockout views of falls and rainbows.
Mosi-oa-Tunya National Park
This compact riverside park protects Zambia's only white rhinos, plus elephants, giraffes, and zebras, on game drives minutes from the falls.
Zambezi River Sunset Cruise
The broad upper Zambezi above the falls glows gold at dusk as hippos grunt and elephants drink, best savored from a classic sundowner boat.
Livingstone Museum
Zambia's oldest and largest museum displays David Livingstone's original letters and journals alongside archaeology, witchcraft exhibits, and Tonga cultural history.
Railway Museum (Zambezi Sawmills Railway Museum)
Vintage steam locomotives and colonial-era rolling stock rust romantically at this open-air collection chronicling the railway that built Livingstone.
Mukuni Village
A 700-year-old Leya village near the falls welcomes visitors for guided walks through homesteads, craft markets, and audiences with local royal traditions.
Batoka Gorge
Below the falls, the Zambezi thrashes through a zigzagging basalt canyon famed for grade-five white-water rafting and soaring views from the rim.

dom.op: Zambia Railways — tickets at Livingstone station, no online booking

train.note: The cross-border train over the Victoria Falls Bridge to Zimbabwe no longer runs as a scheduled passenger service - only the tourist steam excursions cross it. Zambia Railways operates a slow, unreliable service north to Lusaka taking 15 hours or more when it runs; buy at the station on the day. Most people take the bus or fly into Harry Mwanga Nkumbula airport.

intl.to: Victoria Falls (Zimbabwe) - across the Victoria Falls Bridge, ~30 min
intl.op: local shuttle and taxi operators — arranged at the border
Intercape / regional operators — tickets at the Livingstone terminal

bus.note: The Zimbabwe crossing is only 11 km away and is done by taxi or shuttle to the bridge, where you walk or ride across - carry your passport, and consider the KAZA UniVisa which covers both Zambia and Zimbabwe. The Kazungula bridge to Botswana replaced the old ferry in 2021. Domestic coaches to Lusaka take about 7-8 hours on Mazhandu Family Bus and Shalom.

ferry.note: The Kazungula ferry across the Zambezi to Botswana was replaced by a road bridge in 2021, so there is no longer a working vehicle ferry there. Boats on the Zambezi above the falls are sunset cruises and rafting trips below it - excursions rather than transport.

half.name: Zambezi National Park
half.blurb: A game park on the Zimbabwean side of the Zambezi River across the border from Livingstone, with elephant, buffalo, and antelope along the riverbank.

full.name: Chobe National Park
full.blurb: A major wildlife park in Botswana under two hours from Livingstone including border crossing, known for river cruises and dense elephant herds along the Chobe River.
